question: In relation to clopidogrel, it is false that:

options.opa: It is structurally related to thienopyridines.
options.opb: It inhibits adenyl cyclase, and therefore increases cAMP levels.
options.opc: It has a low index of myelotoxicity in relation to ticlopidine.
options.opd: It has a longer action in relation to ticlopidine.
options.ope: In case of surgical intervention, it is recommended to interrupt the treatment at least one week in advance.

analysis: Clopidogrel is a thienopyridine antiplatelet agent that irreversibly inhibits the P2Y12 ADP receptor on platelets, preventing platelet activation and aggregation. It does not inhibit adenyl cyclase, but rather inhibits platelet activation through a different mechanism. Clopidogrel has a lower risk of myelotoxicity compared to ticlopidine. It has a longer duration of action compared to ticlopidine. It is recommended to interrupt clopidogrel treatment at least 5-7 days before elective surgery to minimize bleeding risk.
